messages:
maria: quick check — i'm about to merge a helm values change that scopes a bunch of clusterRoleBindings down to namespace RoleBindings for the `payments` ns. also adding an `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` annotation on the SA via the chart for IRSA. can ppl eyeball?

alex: curious — are we changing service account names or just rebinding existing ones? want to make sure nothing breaks pods that mount secrets by name.

maria: keeping SA names the same (`payments-runner`, `payments-webhook`). only replacement is binding type and adding the annotation on the SA template: 

```yaml
serviceAccount:
  create: true
  name: payments-runner
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-payments-runtime
```

roleBinding snippet in chart: 
```yaml
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: payments-runner-binding
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: payments-runner
  namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: payments-runner-role
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

kai: two small things: 1) we need to ensure TF or our onboarding automation doesn't re-create the ClusterRoleBinding later — do we have a plan to remove the cluster-scoped resource from terraform / iam module? 2) IRSA annotation on an existing SA is fine, but if the SA already has projected tokens disabled, `serviceAccountTokenProjection` config might block OIDC usage.

john: re: (1) i'm working on terraform cleanup in `infra-k8s-rbac` branch. will open a PR today to remove `aws_iam_role`, and move the clusterrolebinding deletion into the migration step. linking plan here: `terraform plan -var='env=prod' -target=module.rbac.cluster_role_binding` — should show removal only.

maria: thanks john. kai — where do we check projected token? i can't find an explicit field in our helm chart.

kai: the kubelet behavior is cluster-level, but for pods it's `spec.serviceAccountTokenProjection` when creating projected volumes. for SA, the kube-apiserver must allow tokenRequest API (which EKS does). Also check existing SA annotation `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` + OIDC provider present. if the SA was created by an older chart that set `automountServiceAccountToken: false` then pods won't get tokens automatically. quick check: `kubectl get sa payments-runner -n payments -o yaml | grep automount`

opsbot: deploy-bot: new release pipeline job `payments/helm:prod` queued by @maria. CI will run `helm template` and `kubeval` for manifests.

sophie: one thing i hit last time — when we switched clusterRoleBinding -> roleBinding we missed a `ClusterRole` rule used by the controller that watches all namespaces. double-check which verbs/resources are needed — sometimes a namespace-scoped Role isn't sufficient for cross-ns controllers.

maria: good call. the role we create only covers secrets/configmaps in `payments` ns. the controller that needs cluster-scope is `cluster-audit` and it keeps using the old cluster rolebinding — i'm going to exclude that controller from this migration. will update the chart values to only migrate service accounts we own.

alex: also quick FYI for rollout: set `strategy.type: RollingUpdate` and small maxUnavailable (10%) — gives us better safety while we confirm token accesses.

maria: plan: 1) john will open TF PR to remove clusterrolebinding. 2) i'll update helm values to add SA annotation + rolebinding only for our ns, exclude `cluster-audit` controllers. 3) i'll run `kubectl get sa payments-runner -n payments -o yaml` after chart deploy and confirm `automountServiceAccountToken` is not false. 4) if all good, merge. will post status here once CI finishes. :thumbsup:

john: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infrastructure/infra-k8s-rbac/pull/42 — includes plan output showing only clusterrolebinding deletion.

maria: thanks folks — CI passed `helm template` and `kubeval` locally, going to stage deploy in `staging` first. ping me if you see any permission errors in staging logs. :eyes:
